text.title: UI Library Advanced Patterns Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on what the surface actually contains — static presentation, an in-flow composite widget, or an overlay layer — and on whether a maintained headless primitive already covers it, to full application, the compound-component half only, or skip.

decision-tree.root-question: What does the surface being built contain: static presentation only, an in-flow composite widget with several focusable parts, or an overlay layer rendered above page content?

branch.when: static presentation only — cards, headings, single buttons, plain form fields; nothing owns focus order or a roving tabindex

conclusion.verdict: skip; there is no focus trap, no shared parent state and no keyboard contract to get wrong, so a compound API adds surface area protecting nothing

branch.when: in-flow composite widget — tabs, accordion, menubar, listbox, combobox — with two or more parts that must share state
branch.question: Have the library's base primitives (Button, Input, tokens) already shipped and stabilised, and is the compound API being authored here rather than wrapped from a vendor?

branch.when: base primitives are still in flux or not shipped

conclusion.verdict: skip; run ui-lib-basics first — a compound API layered over primitives that are still changing gets rewritten with them

branch.when: primitives are stable and the compound API is hand-authored in this library

conclusion.verdict: apply the composition half: root-created context for shared state, a consumer hook that throws a named error outside the provider, and a CSF 3 play function that drives Tab and Arrow keys; the modal rules do not apply

branch.when: the surface renders an overlay — modal dialog, drawer, popover — that covers page content
branch.question: Is a maintained headless primitive (Radix, Headless UI, React Aria) already a dependency, or acceptable to add, for this overlay?

branch.when: yes — a maintained primitive covers this overlay type

conclusion.verdict: skip the hand-rolled path; wrap and style the vendor primitive, then assert only that the six-point focus contract survives your wrapper

branch.when: no — the overlay is hand-rolled in this library and owns its own portal and focus handling

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; the six-point dialog focus contract, the inert background with scroll-lock compensation, and a keyboard-driven play function per pattern are all acceptance criteria
